* Oil prices jumped more than 2% after fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks on ships in the Gulf compounded supply concerns following the closure of a key Saudi oil pipeline.
* Soybeans and corn often track oil prices because of their use in biofuel production.
* U.S. farmers will harvest less corn than previously forecast this autumn, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Friday, after hot summer weather raised concerns about crop damage.

* China bought around 1 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans last week, four traders told Reuters, as the world's top oilseed buyer steps up purchases ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington later this month.
* The grains market is also closely monitoring risks in the Black Sea region, where Russia and Ukraine have sharply escalated attacks on each other's shipping in recent weeks.

* Following drone strikes, Russian authorities suspended navigation in the Sea of Azov in early July, while an August 12 attack halted loading operations at key terminals at Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea port.

* Argentine soybean sales are gaining pace as farmers move to lock in prices after a sharp rally fueled by strong Chinese demand for supplies and mounting concerns over the U.S. crop, the Rosario grains exchange said in a report on Friday.
* Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn, soy and wheat, traders said on Friday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
